text: Why is it that product management is still such a relatively undeveloped discipline? We're like 15 to 20 years into this, and so there's something about the current state of product management that isn't getting at the truly important things, the truly value-added things.
speaker: Shaun Clowes
context: Lenny asks Shaun about his strong opinions on the state of product management and how most PMs are not that great. Shaun is reflecting on why product management as a discipline hasn't matured as much as it should have after 15-20 years. He explains that there's something fundamentally wrong with how product management is currently practiced, as it's not focusing on the truly valuable and important aspects of the role, leading to random outcomes and performance.
text_ko: 왜 아직도 프로덕트 매니지먼트(product management)가 이렇게 비교적 덜 발달한 분야일까요? 벌써 15~20년이나 지났는데도, 지금의 프로덕트 매니지먼트에는 진짜 중요한 것들이나 진짜 가치를 만들어내는 부분에 제대로 다가가지 못하는 뭔가가 있는 것 같아요.
text_zh: 为什么产品管理(product management)到现在还算是个相对不成熟的领域？我们也折腾了差不多15到20年了，但现在的产品管理好像没抓住那些真正重要、真正能创造价值的点儿。
text_es: ¿Por qué la gestión de producto (product management) sigue siendo una disciplina tan poco desarrollada? Ya llevamos entre 15 y 20 años en esto, y hay algo en su estado actual que no está llegando a lo que de verdad importa, a lo que realmente aporta valor.
key_sentence: Product management remains a relatively undeveloped discipline, missing truly value-added things.
original_text: Why is it that product management is still such a relatively undeveloped discipline? We're like 15 to 20 years into this, and so there's something about the current state of product management that isn't getting at the truly important things, the truly value-added things. If we were doctors, you'd be like, "That's totally unacceptable."

vocabulary.definition: Lacking in growth, progress, or maturity; not fully formed or realized.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'undeveloped' often refers to markets, products, or sectors that have not yet reached their potential or are in the early stages of evolution.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'undeveloped' can imply a lack of sophistication, it may also suggest potential for growth and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: A field of study or branch of knowledge characterized by a specific set of principles and practices.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'discipline' can refer to areas of expertise, such as marketing, finance, or product management, each with its own methodologies and frameworks.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a structured approach to a field, but may also suggest rigidity in thinking or practice if not balanced with creativity.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to enhancements or features that increase the worth of a product or service beyond its basic function.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'value-added' is often used to describe services or features that differentiate a product in the marketplace and justify a higher price point.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'value-added' typically has a positive connotation, it can be overused or misapplied to features that do not genuinely enhance customer experience.

vocabulary.definition: Of great significance or value; having a major effect on outcomes or decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'important' is often used to prioritize tasks, initiatives, or strategies that will have a substantial impact on organizational success.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'important' is a straightforward term, its effectiveness can be diminished if overused; specificity can enhance clarity.

text: In everything always talk from the customer's perspective, from the market's perspective, from the competitor's perspective, the very small number of PMs do that.
speaker: Shaun Clowes
context: Lenny asks Shaun for the solution to help PMs level up and become great product managers. Shaun explains that the fundamental problem is most PMs spend too much time looking inside the building rather than outside. He emphasizes that PMs should always start from external perspectives - customer, market, and competitor viewpoints - but most get distracted by internal operational tasks and politics, which prevents them from being truly effective.
text_ko: 무엇을 하든 항상 고객 관점에서, 시장 관점에서, 경쟁자 관점에서 말해보세요. 그렇게 하는 제품 관리자들(PMs)은 정말 극소수예요.
text_zh: 所有事情都要从客户、市场和竞争对手的角度来说，可真正这么做的产品经理（PMs）寥寥无几。
text_es: En todo lo que hagas, habla siempre desde la perspectiva del cliente, del mercado y de la competencia. Muy pocos responsables de producto (PMs) lo hacen.
key_sentence: the very small number of PMs do that.
original_text: In everything always talk from the customer's perspective, from the market's perspective, from the competitor's perspective, the very small number of PMs do that. They get dragged into internal politics, they get dragged into scrum management or scrum execution or product delivery, and you just can't win that way.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of considering something; a viewpoint.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding different perspectives—such as those of customers, competitors, and the market—is crucial for making informed decisions and developing effective strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'perspective' often implies a subjective viewpoint, it can also suggest a broader understanding when used in strategic discussions.

text: Well, you've got this synthesis machine, which is this LLM thing that's going to help you do synthesis, but if it hasn't got all that data to do synthesis on top of, it's got nothing.
speaker: Shaun Clowes
context: Lenny asks about Shaun's hot take that AI will most impact product management through data management rather than models. Shaun explains that LLMs are essentially synthesis machines - they're very good at analyzing and synthesizing information, but they're completely dependent on the quality and recency of data fed to them. Without good data input, even the smartest LLM produces nothing valuable, making data management the critical bottleneck for AI success.
text_ko: 있잖아요, 합성 도구(synthesis machine)가 있고 그게 합성을 도와주는 대형 언어 모델(LLM) 같은 건데, 그걸로 합성할 데이터가 충분히 없으면 아무것도 못 해요.
text_zh: 你现在有个用来做合成的“机器”，也就是那个大模型(LLM)，本来能帮你把东西整合起来，但要是没有数据让它去整合，那它就派不上用场。
text_es: Mira, tienes una especie de máquina de síntesis (synthesis machine), que es un modelo de lenguaje (LLM) que te ayuda a sintetizar, pero si no cuenta con todos esos datos sobre los que sintetizar, no tiene nada.
key_sentence: if it hasn't got all that data to do synthesis on top of, it's got nothing.
original_text: Well, you've got this synthesis machine, which is this LLM thing that's going to help you do synthesis, but if it hasn't got all that data to do synthesis on top of, it's got nothing. And so that means that LLMs can only be as good as the data they are given and how recent that data is.

vocabulary.definition: The process of combining different ideas, influences, or objects to form a coherent whole.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, synthesis often refers to the integration of diverse data sources or insights to develop innovative solutions or strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While synthesis implies a constructive merging of elements, it should not be confused with mere aggregation, which lacks the depth of integration.

text: People really underestimate where the value is created in these applications and they just kind of get it completely wrong.
speaker: Shaun Clowes
context: Lenny asks about the future of B2B SaaS businesses if AI makes it easy to clone applications like Salesforce or Atlassian - whether these companies will be in trouble. Shaun responds that people fundamentally misunderstand where the real value lies in these enterprise applications. He's setting up to explain that the value isn't just in the user interface or basic functionality that can be easily replicated, but in something much deeper and harder to clone.
text_ko: 사람들이 이런 애플리케이션(applications)에서 가치가 실제로 어디서 창출되는지를 정말 과소평가하고, 그래서 그냥 완전히 잘못 판단해요.
text_zh: 大家真的是小看了这些应用程序的价值到底在哪儿创造出来的，基本上是完全搞错了方向。
text_es: La gente de verdad no entiende dónde se genera el valor en estas aplicaciones y simplemente se equivocan por completo.
key_sentence: People really underestimate where value is created and get it completely wrong.

vocabulary.definition: To assess something as less significant or less capable than it actually is.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, underestimating a competitor's strength or market potential can lead to strategic miscalculations and missed opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of insight or awareness; it is best used when discussing misjudgments in evaluations.

vocabulary.definition: The importance, worth, or usefulness of something, often quantified in monetary terms.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, value can refer to the perceived benefits of a product or service that drive customer demand and revenue generation.
vocabulary.nuance: Value can be subjective, varying between different stakeholders; it is important to specify whether you are discussing intrinsic, market, or perceived value.

vocabulary.definition: The practical uses or implementations of a product, service, or technology in real-world scenarios.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, applications often refer to software programs designed to perform specific tasks for users, enhancing productivity or solving problems.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'applications' can refer to software, it can also encompass broader uses of technology in various industries; clarity is key when discussing specific contexts.

vocabulary.definition: To a full or entire extent; wholly or entirely without exception.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communications, using 'completely' can emphasize totality, such as in project completion or adherence to guidelines.
vocabulary.nuance: While it conveys thoroughness, overuse may come off as redundant; it is best used when absolute certainty is intended.

text: They get dragged into internal politics, they get dragged into scrum management or scrum execution or product delivery, like elements of the delivery thing and you just can't win that way. You just can't win that way.
speaker: Shaun Clowes
context: Lenny asks Shaun what makes PMs become great 10x product managers. Shaun explains that the biggest mistake most PMs make is spending time on internal operational tasks rather than focusing on external market insights. He emphasizes that PMs who get caught up in delivery mechanics and internal politics cannot achieve excellence because they're not addressing the core job of product management, which is finding reliable, differentiated value in the market.
text_ko: 그들은 사내 정치에 휘말리고, 스크럼 관리(scrum management)나 스크럼 실행(scrum execution), 제품 딜리버리(product delivery) 같은 딜리버리 관련 업무에 끌려 들어가요. 그렇게 해서는 이길 수가 없어요. 정말 이길 수가 없어요.
text_zh: 你会被卷进内部政治，也会被拉去处理Scrum管理（scrum management）、Scrum执行（scrum execution）或者产品交付（product delivery）这些交付环节的事儿，这样根本赢不了，真的赢不了。
text_es: Se ven arrastrados a la política interna, a la gestión o a la ejecución de Scrum (scrum management, scrum execution) o a la entrega del producto (product delivery), a elementos del proceso de entrega, y así no se puede ganar. No se puede ganar así.
key_sentence: You just can't win that way.
original_text: They get dragged into internal politics, they get dragged into scrum management or scrum execution or product delivery, like elements of the delivery thing and you just can't win that way. You just can't win that way. You can never get an A because you're fundamentally not solving the job.

vocabulary.definition: The dynamics and power struggles that occur within an organization, often involving competing interests and agendas among employees or departments.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, internal politics can influence decision-making, resource allocation, and employee morale, often hindering collaboration and efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: While internal politics can be a natural part of organizational life, excessive involvement can lead to conflicts and distract from core business objectives.

vocabulary.definition: The process of bringing a product from development to the end user, encompassing all stages from design to distribution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, effective product delivery is crucial for meeting customer expectations and achieving market success, often involving agile methodologies and iterative feedback.
vocabulary.nuance: Product delivery emphasizes not just the final output but also the efficiency and effectiveness of the processes involved in getting the product to market.

text: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from. So avoid availability or confirmation bias.
speaker: Shaun Clowes
context: Lenny asks how someone can recognize if they're actually not doing enough external research, even if they think they are. Shaun explains that many PMs claim to talk to customers and look at data frequently, but they fall into the trap of only seeking familiar sources and perspectives. He emphasizes the importance of actively seeking out unfamiliar viewpoints and challenging your own assumptions to avoid confirmation bias and truly learn something new.
text_ko: 밖을 많이 살펴본다고 말하는 건 한 가지예요. 평소에 잘 듣지 못하던 곳의 목소리를 실제로 듣는 건 완전히 다른 얘기예요. 그러니까 가용성 편향(availability bias)이나 확증 편향(confirmation bias)에 빠지지 않도록 하세요.
text_zh: 说自己花很多时间走出去看外面的情况是一回事，能真正听到那些平时接触不到的声音又是另外一回事。所以别被可得性偏差(availability bias)或确认偏差(confirmation bias)牵着走。
text_es: Una cosa es decir que pasas mucho tiempo mirando fuera de la empresa; otra muy distinta es escuchar a quienes normalmente no escuchas. Evita el sesgo de disponibilidad (availability bias) y el sesgo de confirmación (confirmation bias).
key_sentence: It's a whole other thing to hear from places avoiding availability or confirmation bias.
original_text: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from. So avoid availability or confirmation bias. Most of the time people go talk to the people they always talk to and they learn nothing particularly new.

vocabulary.definition: Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for, interpret, and remember information in a way that confirms one’s preexisting beliefs or hypotheses.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, confirmation bias can hinder innovation and critical analysis, as teams may overlook contradictory evidence that could lead to better outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: This bias can be particularly detrimental in strategic planning and market research, where an objective assessment of data is crucial; awareness of it can foster more rigorous evaluation processes.
